title: Developer Experience Docs Playbook — SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples & Top Support Issues
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook documents the standard approach the Developer Experience (DevX) team uses to author, review, publish, and maintain SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical fixes for top support issues. The goal is consistency across languages, fast time-to-first-success for users, and a single source of truth for commonly reported support problems.

Scope

- SDK guides (Python, TypeScript/Node, Go, Java)
- Quickstarts and one-file templates for common integrations (chat, embeddings, streaming, file-based retrieval)
- API examples used by docs site and SDK README snippets
- Docs-site operating procedures (publishing, versioning, redirects, search indexing)
- Top support issues and canonical fixes (triaged and maintained by DevX + Support)

Owner and Roles

- Primary owner: DevX docs team (engineering)
- Reviewers: SDK owners, security (when auth changes), product for new feature messaging
- Escalation: Customer Success -> DevX -> SDK Owner -> Product

1) Docs-site operating procedures

Purpose: Ensure changes to the documentation website are reviewed, validated, and deployed with minimal user impact.

Checklist for publishing a new doc or example

1. Draft in markdown following the docs-site front-matter template (see Templates section).
2. Run local preview: npm run start-docs (or make start-docs).
3. Validate code snippets: run `./scripts/snippet-checker --lang python` to verify code compiles and lints.
4. Add test case in docs-integration-ci for any runnable sample (CI will run short smoke tests).
5. Submit PR with the following checklist in PR description: scope, risk, owner, reviewers, test plan, and related product ticket.
6. At least one SDK owner + one reviewer must approve.
7. Merge and wait for automated deploy to staging; QA sign-off required before promoting to prod.

Versioning and stable references

- Docs are versioned by major API release (e.g., v1, v2). The default docs site shows latest stable.
- Use permanent permalinks for examples that may be referenced by customers; add redirects when examples move.
- When changing an example that will break existing customer code, add a migration section and mark change as a breaking change in the PR.

Search indexing and metadata

- Add the following front-matter fields for each doc: title, summary, tags, language (if code-specific), examples (list of example IDs).
- To improve search, add relevant labels (up to 6) and common synonyms in a hidden 'keywords' field.

2) SDK guides and quickstarts (authoring standards)

Authoring principles

- Start with a short goal statement: what success looks like in <5 minutes.
- Provide a complete minimal example that can be copy-pasted and run without alteration (except for API key).
- Include a short explanation of key concepts after the runnable example (why defaults were chosen).
- Add a troubleshooting section with 3-5 common errors and fixes.

Quickstart template (recommended structure)

1. Title and 1-line objective
2. Prerequisites (SDK version, minimum language/runtime, API key env var)
3. Minimal runnable example (with comments)
4. How it works — short explanation of payloads/flows
5. Next steps and links to full SDK guide

Example: Python chat quickstart (minimal)

```python
# quickstart: chat
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.chat.create(model='redwood-1b', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Hello!'}])
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```

3) API examples and snippet hygiene

Standards for any code snippet used in docs or SDK READMEs

- Snippets must be <= 40 lines for readability; longer examples go into the examples repo with a short snippet in the docs that links to the full example.
- Do not include long secrets or customer data. Use placeholders and `os.getenv` pattern for auth.
- Include language-specific best practices (async/await for JS examples when using streaming; context managers in Python for session cleanup).
- Add a one-line comment explaining expected output where helpful.

API example (HTTP curl)

curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -d '{"model":"redwood-1b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the following text..."}]}'

4) Top support issues & canonical fixes (current list)

This list is maintained jointly with Support. Each entry includes problem, root cause, canonical fix, and escalation notes. Update cadence: quarterly or after major platform changes.

- Issue: SDK authentication failures (invalid token or 401)
  - Symptoms: 401 or 403 responses in first API call; SDK raises AuthenticationError.
  - Canonical fix: Ensure REDWOOD_API_KEY is set and does not contain trailing whitespace. Run: `echo -n $REDWOOD_API_KEY | wc -c` and `jq -R . <<< \"$REDWOOD_API_KEY\"` to inspect characters. If using CI, check secrets manager path and permissions.
  - Escalation: If token is valid and server still responds 401, collect request-id header and escalate to infra oncall.

- Issue: Streaming responses stall after 1-2 tokens
  - Symptoms: Client receives initial tokens then stalls; no final end-of-stream event.
  - Canonical fix: Confirm client uses the SDK streaming helpers (e.g., client.chat.stream()) and that network layer allows long-lived connections (idle timeouts). For Node, ensure keepAlive: true in HTTP agent. For Kubernetes ingress, confirm proxy_read_timeout >= 120s.
  - Escalation: Capture tcpdump/trace, attach request-id, and open support ticket.

- Issue: Mismatch in token counting / billing expectations
  - Symptoms: Customer reports token usage higher than expected.
  - Canonical fix: Explain difference between input tokens, output tokens, and internal model tokens (system tokens). Share snippet to replicate tokenization using our tokenizer tool: `python -m redwood.tokenizer \"text\"`. For SDKs, include utility `client.tokens.estimate()` examples.

- Issue: Example code not runnable or fails in CI
  - Symptoms: Docs-integration CI fails on snippet-checker or unit/regression tests.
  - Canonical fix: Reproduce locally using snippet-runner, fix formatting/indentation, pin minimal dependencies in example requirements (e.g., requests==2.31.*). Add a CI test that runs the example script in a sandbox.

5) Templates & repository structure

Required front-matter for new examples (YAML-style)

| field | required | notes |
| title | yes | Short, unique example title |
| id | yes | short-kebab-id used for permalinks |
| language | yes | python | typescript | go | java |
| runtime | optional | e.g., node16, python3.11 |
| test | optional | path to ci smoke test |

Template file (markdown) header example:

---
title: Chat quickstart (Python)
id: chat-quickstart-python
language: python
---

Reusable skeletons live in docs/examples/templates/, and runnable examples live in examples/repos/<language>/. Add a README.md to each examples folder explaining how to run locally and in CI.

6) Maintenance & review cadence

- Weekly: Triage new doc-related support tickets and add to backlog if they indicate a common pattern.
- Monthly: Run snippet-checker across the site and resolve failures.
- Quarterly: Full audit of quickstarts and SDK guides to ensure compatibility with latest SDK releases and platform changes.

7) Troubleshooting playbook for oncall DevX

Steps to triage a docs-related customer report:

1. Reproduce the problem against the latest docs commit (use staging docs if possible).
2. Run snippet-checker / snippet-runner for the failing snippet.
3. If reproduction fails, ask customer for exact error, SDK version, and request-id (if API call).
4. If failure is in example only, patch the example, add a regression test, and backport if necessary.
5. If failure is platform or SDK-related, open a JIRA linking to customer report and notify SDK owner.

Appendix A — Example bug-fix PR checklist for examples

- [ ] Reproduced locally
- [ ] Added/updated smoke test to docs-integration-ci
- [ ] Updated front-matter or metadata if example ID changed
- [ ] Reviewer: SDK owner + DevX tech lead
- [ ] Changelog entry if required

Appendix B — Useful CLI commands

- Local docs preview: `npm run start-docs`
- Snippet lint: `./scripts/snippet-checker --lang all`
- Run a specific example: `python examples/python/chat_quickstart.py`
- Token estimate: `python -m redwood.tokenizer 'your text'`

Contacts and escalation

- DevX docs lead: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
- SDK owners: see OWNERS file in each SDK repo
- Support triage queue: support-triage@redwood.ai

Change log
